module: inspect.lua 3.1.0: third-party library (Enrique García Cota, MIT license) that turns any Lua value into a readable string: sorted tables, indentation, circular references marked by <id>, metatables displayed. The module is callable: inspect(t, options). Handy for debugging.
usage:
local inspect = require("libs/inspect/inspect")
print(inspect({1, 2, a = {b = true}}, {depth = 2}))
notes: Options of inspect.inspect: depth (max depth, unlimited by default), newline (default "\n"), indent (default two spaces), process (function process(item, path) applied recursively before display).
Functions, userdata and threads are displayed in the form <type id>.
The KEY and METATABLE fields are internal markers used in process (inferred from code).
`i` is listed as an assigned global by the automatic extractor; in practice it is a local loop variable of the file (to be checked, not essential).

inspect.desc: Returns a textual representation of root. Can also be called directly: inspect(root, options).

KEY.desc: Key marker used in the path passed to options.process.

METATABLE.desc: Metatable marker used in the path passed to options.process.

Inspector.desc: Internal object that accumulates text in a buffer while walking the value.

puts.desc: Appends pieces of text to the buffer.

tabify.desc: Appends a line break followed by the indentation of the current level.

down.desc: Runs f one level deeper (increments then decrements the level).

alreadyVisited.desc: Tells whether the value already has an identifier (table already encountered).

getId.desc: Returns the numeric identifier of the value, according to its type, creating it if needed.

putKey.desc: Writes a table key: raw identifier or [key] in brackets.

putTable.desc: Writes a table: sequential and non-sequential parts, metatable, depth limit, repeated references.

putValue.desc: Writes a value according to its type (escaped string, number, boolean, table, or <type id>).
